title: Modernize route resolver, introduce shard-aware fallbacks and reduce hotpath locking
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The smart routing layer has accrued multiple hotpath patches over the last 18 months: a global route cache guarded by a coarse lock, two ad-hoc fallback implementations (legacy synchronous fallback + newer async proxy) and region-specific heuristics duplicated across three modules. This caused intermittent latency spikes under bursty traffic and made it difficult to reason about fallbacks and capacity-sensitive routing behavior.

This ticket refactors the route resolver and fallback coordinator with three goals: 1) remove a global lock from the runtime hotpath, 2) unify fallback logic into a shard-aware coordinator that respects regional capacity leases, and 3) modernize telemetry so regressions are detectable by per-route unit tests and dashboards. Work includes small dependency bumps needed for lock-free concurrent maps and observability helpers.
acceptance_criteria: Route evaluation no longer takes a global mutex on the serving hotpath (verified via code review and stress tests)
Fallback coordinator is replaced with shard-aware coordinator that prioritizes local-region capacity and exposes a fallback decision trace in traces and logs
Unit + integration tests cover at least 95% of route-evaluation branches and fallback paths
Performance: p50 route selection latency improvement >= 20% on benchmark harness; p99 latency not regressing vs baseline
New telemetry emitted: routing.route_eval_ms, routing.fallback_count, routing.fallback_latency_ms, routing.shard_lease_retries; dashboards updated (link in attachments)
Docs: engineering runbook updated with decision flow and troubleshooting steps for fallback behavior
tasks: Design: document shard-aware fallback algorithm and failure modes (done)
Prototype: replace global cache with sharded concurrent map and microbenchmark (in progress)
Refactor: extract single fallback coordinator and remove legacy sync fallback code path
Tests: add property-based tests to validate fallback fairness and lease behavior
Observability: add metrics + tracing tags and update console dashboard
Release: staged rollout with feature flag and canary traffic for 48 hours
comments: 2026-01-19 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff doc uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/~apatel/shard-aware-routing. High-level trade-offs: per-shard locks vs lock-free maps; we prefer sharded locks to simplify correctness for now.
2026-01-22 - Marco Liu: Prototype microbenchmarks on m5-large-style machine show route-eval p50 24ms -> 18ms using 16-way sharding; allocations drop ~28%.
2026-01-28 - Review from Priya Nambiar (SRE): Concern about lease heartbeat frequency contributing to chattiness; decided to use exponential backoff and jitter (see design section 3).
2026-02-02 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8123 (sharded-route-cache + tests). Waiting on cross-repo integration tests.
2026-02-05 - Nick O. (Runtime): Suggested upgrading concurrent-map dependency to v2 to fix a GC churn bug; accepted and added to PR. Note: bump requires go.mod tidy and run `make bench`.
2026-02-10 - QA: Integration run against staging traffic replay shows fallback_count reduced by 42% during simulated regional outage and p99 route-selection latency improved from 112ms -> 76ms.
2026-02-12 - Product feedback (Lina H.): Good outcome for reliability; requested a small dashboard tile exposing per-customer fallback_rate for enterprise customers. Added as follow-up.
Implementation notes: keep legacy sync fallback code behind feature-flag 'legacy_fallback' for two weeks post-rollout to allow quick rollback.
decision_log: Prefer sharded route cache (16 shards) with per-shard RW locks over fully lock-free structure to reduce complexity and bugs in initial rollout
Unify fallback logic into a single coordinator that uses region leases and capacity signals; fallback decisions annotated with trace ids for post-mortem analysis
Schedule dependency upgrades in separate small PRs: concurrent-map v2, observability helper v1.4; keep Go runtime upgrade out of scope for this ticket
Canary rollout: feature-flag gating + 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 48h windows and automatic rollback on SLA breaches
notes: Edge cases to watch: (1) stale shard leases when region controllers restart, (2) double-fallback storms when multiple regions report low capacity within the same decision window. We'll add throttling and observable counters for both.
follow_up: Add per-customer fallback rate dashboard (requested by PM)
Plan a separate ticket to migrate legacy sync fallback code out of the repo after 2-week observation window
Re-evaluate sharding factor after 1 week of production telemetry and adjust if contention remains
